theme: 3 terms on arrays in depth: a view into part of an array, setting space aside before appending, and an array that always sits side by side in memory

terms.definition: A view into part of an array, made with a range, that shares the array's storage and keeps its original indices.
terms.example: `recent` is an ArraySlice, so its first index isn't zero.
terms.code:
let scores = [10, 20, 30, 40]
let top = scores[1...2]
print(top)
print(top.startIndex)

terms.definition: Calling `reserveCapacity` to set aside room for a number of items before you append them, so the array grows only once.
terms.example: We know there are a thousand rows, so Reserve Capacity first.
terms.code:
var ids: [Int] = []
ids.reserveCapacity(1000)
for i in 0..<1000 { ids.append(i) }
print(ids.count)
print(ids.capacity >= 1000)

terms.definition: An array type that always stores its items side by side in one block of memory, which can make it a bit faster.
terms.example: Switch to ContiguousArray only if Instruments shows the loop is slow.
terms.code:
var points = ContiguousArray<Double>()
points.append(1.5)
points.append(2.5)
print(points.reduce(0, +))

quizzes.question: What do you call setting aside room for items before you append them?
In this code, what type is `part`, which keeps the indices from `all`?
Which array type always stores its items side by side in one block of memory?

video.description:
Learn to explain arrays in depth: ArraySlice, Reserve Capacity & ContiguousArray, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ArraySlice - A view into part of an array, made with a range, that shares the array's storage and keeps its original indices.
Reserve Capacity - Calling `reserveCapacity` to set aside room for a number of items before you append them, so the array grows only once.
ContiguousArray - An array type that always stores its items side by side in one block of memory, which can make it a bit faster.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift ArraySlice, Reserve Capacity & ContiguousArray | Day 61
landscape.description:
Explain ArraySlice, Reserve Capacity & ContiguousArray in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
배열 슬라이스, 용량 예약, 연속 배열 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

ArraySlice - A view into part of an array, made with a range, that shares the array's storage and keeps its original indices.
한국어: 배열 슬라이스: 범위로 만든 배열의 일부분으로, 원래 배열의 저장 공간과 인덱스를 그대로 공유함

Reserve Capacity - Calling `reserveCapacity` to set aside room for a number of items before you append them, so the array grows only once.
한국어: 용량 예약: `reserveCapacity`로 append 전에 필요한 개수만큼 공간을 미리 잡아 배열이 한 번만 커지게 하는 것

ContiguousArray - An array type that always stores its items side by side in one block of memory, which can make it a bit faster.
한국어: ContiguousArray: 항목을 항상 메모리의 한 블록에 나란히 저장해서 조금 더 빠를 수 있는 배열 타입

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why index zero crashed on a slice, why the buffer reserves space first and when a special array type is worth it, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Why did index zero crash? Can you explain it in English?

dialogue.title: Index zero crashed

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `recent[0]` crashed. But `recent` has three items!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `recent` is an ArraySlice. It keeps the indices from `all`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So its first index is 2, not 0?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. With an ArraySlice, use `first` or `startIndex`, never zero.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Reserve Capacity sets the space aside once, before we append.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the array doesn't grow again and again?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Reserve Capacity saves those extra copies when you know the size.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And why is `buffer` a ContiguousArray, not a normal array?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A ContiguousArray keeps items side by side in memory, so it can be faster.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK, but I'd measure first before I use ContiguousArray everywhere.

dialogue.code:
let all = [5, 8, 2, 9, 4]
let recent = all[2...]
var buffer = ContiguousArray<Int>()
buffer.reserveCapacity(all.count)
buffer.append(contentsOf: recent)

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's an ArraySlice. It keeps the old indices.
